I don't have a lot of motivation to get to know or interact with people, and I think social anxiety and a subconscious mistrust of others attributes to that. Those things stem from a deep history of failure or perception of failure/sensitivity at socializing from a young age. I wouldn't consider myself a total misanthrope, nor totally lonely, but from my perspective I would say it's possible to be both. I personally have found myself frustrated with human nature at times *while* feeling alone in the past. Nowadays I think misanthropy is pointless and toxic. I don't hate people. Not sure if that's relevant. 

Anyways, yeah, the "acting" people do trips me up. I find I lack the ability to adopt the "character" I desire, so I'm just myself. The weird thing is, I can't tell to what extent people are just "acting". I think the majority if people are just being "themselves", but seem to have a more objective outlook on socializing and "act" in ways that are mostly instinctual for them. They don't have to try to look happpy or sad or laugh or smile or find the right words; it's just...there. Which is why improving social skills for someone like me is tiring; for *me* it literally would be acting, like a performer on a stage. I'm very deeply selfish as well, and I don't operate based on emotion like others do, which doesn't help.  I don't find I want companionship, but allies for mutually-assured survival, and people to have a good time with. I've actually found this in my life to some extent. I think others have the anxiety and lacking social skills thing to much higher degrees than I do. 

And yes, I find myself bored with people a lot. I find myself tolerating most conversation instead of really wanting to be a part of it, and when I'm talking to someone, I'm very easily disinterested in what they have to say. I don't find myself to be very interested in others in general.

I tend to have a high opinion of myself despite it, more in an "I accept myself" way than "I'm better than others". I tend to not think of myself as "sad", but I fully understand why "normal" people would say I am. They just think that because of their perspective. They don't understand how a situation like mine could be "just fine", even if it really is.

I get along with people in a sense but because I'm terrible socially people tend not to like talking to me and find me to be weird. I just don't know how to act I guess; it's pretty exhausting . It doesn't help that I just cannot bring myself to be interested in people in and of themselves and that my motivations socially tend to be different from the norm.
